title: Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

reading.body:
An AI image generation system was used to create and distribute non-consensual sexual imagery of a real person. The deployment failure was the absence of any check on what the system produced or how the output would be used. The person operating it obtained source photographs without consent and distributed the generated images across multiple platforms using fake accounts to conceal his identity.

What is not established: whether the AI system had safeguards against this use, whether those safeguards failed, or whether the operator circumvented them.

The failure shows a gap between what image generation tools can do and the social harms they enable when deployed without accountability. Detection happened only after the victim was alerted by others who saw the images being shared. Earlier intervention would have required either the AI system to refuse the request, the platform distributing it to detect and block it, or human review at any point in the chain before circulation began.

reports.title: Delhi: Man held for circulating obscene AI-generated photos of college acquaintance
Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

summary:
A 22-year-old man named Keshav Bansal was arrested in Delhi for creating and spreading obscene AI-generated images of a female college acquaintance. Bansal, a BTech graduate in Electronics and Communication Engineering, obtained photographs from the woman's private social media accounts and used artificial intelligence technology to generate sexually explicit morphed images. He then distributed this content through multiple fake accounts on Instagram, Discord, and Facebook while using various Gmail addresses to hide his identity.

The victim discovered the harassment when she received messages from anonymous Instagram accounts alerting her to the morphed photographs and videos being shared on Discord servers. She filed a complaint with the Cyber Police Station in North Delhi, which launched an investigation. Police analyzed digital footprints and traced connections between the fake profiles, eventually identifying and apprehending Bansal. During interrogation, he admitted that personal resentment from college had motivated his actions. Police recovered his mobile phone, SIM cards, and other digital evidence, with investigations continuing.
